_comment: Gzip limits (level 9) for the production build, enforced by scripts/check-budgets.mjs. Measured 22 Nov 2026 on one laptop for the interface rebuild with a dark theme (see docs/performance.md): first-load JS 112.3 kB, first-load CSS 9.5 kB, largest lazy chunk 36.0 kB (Call), largest CSS file 8.1 kB (the entry stylesheet), no fonts. The limits before this rebuild were 110, 8, 38 and 6 kB, passed at 109.3, 7.2, 30.3 and 5.8 kB. They were raised for what the rebuild added: an authored dark theme (the token stylesheet went from 3.3 to 5.9 kB, and every page downloads it), the theme runtime and the header's sliding indicator, which are part of the first load, and richer call and report screens (the call chunk is 5.7 kB larger). On 23 Nov 2026 the largest-lazy-chunk limit went from 38 to 40 kB, and only that one: the call chunk grew from 36.3 to 38.9 kB for hands-free listening (about 1 kB of logic: restartable recognition sessions, Firefly's own end-of-turn wait, idle ticks) and for the screen of a call (the presence ring, live captions and the call-ended moment: about 1.5 kB). The other three limits stayed, and the build now measures 112.9, 10.1 and 8.6 kB against them. Each limit is the measured value plus roughly 1 to 2 kB, so a barrel, the voice catalogue or a chart library moving into the entry chunk is still noticed. Fonts, source maps, extra pages and zod are not budgeted: they are not allowed at all. Raising a limit is a decision: say why in the commit.
